Definition: from G2818; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession:--inheritance.
KeyPassages: Matthew 21:38; Mark 12:7; Luke 12:13; Acts 7:5; Galatians 3:18; Ephesians 1:14
BiblicalUsage: Kleronomia is the inheritance itself, the heirship. Matthew 21:38 and Mark 12:7 have the husbandmen saying, this is the heir, come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance, Luke 12:13 has a man asking Jesus to divide the inheritance with his brother, Acts 7:5 says God gave Abraham none inheritance in the land, yet promised it to his seed, Galatians 3:18 says if the inheritance be of the law, it is no more of promise, but God gave it to Abraham by promise, and Ephesians 1:14 calls the Spirit the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the inheritance is the whole gospel in one word: promised to Abraham, refused by the husbandmen, divided by brothers, and sealed by the Spirit. I hold that Galatians 3:18 settles it forever, because what comes by promise cannot come by law.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Mark; Luke; Acts; Galatians; Ephesians
